Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: the grace days, the late fee, the days for each reminder step, the deposit share, the overdue amount you accept and the days you want clients to pay within.
Check Clients and Payment Terms: every client has a type, terms in days and a pay method. A labour hour is one cleaner working for one hour and a crew is the cleaners who work together on a job.

Write each invoice on Invoices: the client, the jobs, the amount and the due date. The balance, the days overdue, the days to pay and the payment timing fill in by themselves; the Invoice Builder works out the amount and the due date first.
Record every payment on Payments and the weekly totals on Cash Received by Week; a part payment keeps the invoice open with the balance that remains.
Each month open Billing Runs and Invoice Lines to check what was billed and at what price per job and per labour hour.
Follow the reminder ladder on Reminders Sent: write the step, the channel and the outcome of every reminder; the schedule check tells you when one went out late.
Use Collection Calls for clients who do not pay, write the promised date and mark whether the promise was kept.
Open Credit Notes, Disputed Invoices, Write-offs, Payment Plans and Deposits for the cases that change an invoice, and Statements Sent for the monthly statements.
Read Aging Buckets, Late Payers and Direct Debit Runs to see how old the unpaid invoices are, who pays late and how often a collection fails.
Use the 14 calculators when you plan: invoice, late fee, days outstanding, aging, reminders, deposits, plans, credits, risk, forecast, discounts, direct debit, write-offs and a what-if grid.
Read the Billing Dashboard and Charts every week. Tax, late fee and collection rules differ by place: check your own local rules before you use any sample wording.

Complaints with days open and the response check
One row per complaint with the job, client, crew, kind, priority, handler, credit and response time; the days open, the resolved-in-time check and the phones fill in.
Re-cleans with the cost against the job price
One row per free return visit with the job, client, reason, labour hours (one cleaner working for one hour), cost and crew; the cost share of the job price fills in.
Cost share of the job price
Reviews with days to reply and the low rating flag
One row per review with the job, client, crew, source, rating, topic and reply; the stars, the days to reply, the low rating flag and the phones fill in by themselves.
Yearly office contracts with days to the end
One row per contract term with the client, dates, visits, monthly value, yearly increase and status; the days to the end, yearly value and renewal check fill in.
Clients with months active and the retention check
The clients with type, frequency, price, start, status, lead source and the day they left; the monthly value, months active and retention check fill in by themselves.
Service credits with the days after the complaint
One row per credit given to a client with the complaint, the reason, the amount and who approved it; the days after the complaint and the phones fill in by themselves.
Review replies with the days after the review
One row per reply to a review with the day, who wrote it and the tone; the client, the stars and the days after the review fill in by themselves.
Lost and paused clients with the value lost per year
One row per client who left or paused with the day, the reason, the months they stayed and the monthly value; the value lost per year and the phones fill in by themselves.
Referrals with the reward and the months to the first visit
One row per client who brought a new client with the day, the reward and the day it was paid; the first visit, the months to the first visit and the reward check fill in by themselves.
One row per step of a renewal (reminder, price proposal, call, signature) with the day, who did it and the outcome; the client, end date and days to the end fill in.
Visits due and done for each contract week
One row per week of a contract with the visits due, the visits done and any issue; the visits missed, the visit check and the client fill in by themselves.
Satisfaction surveys with the overall score
One row per survey answer with the client and the scores from 1 to 5 for quality, punctuality, communication and value; the overall score and the phones fill in by themselves.
Root causes of complaints with the days to fix
One row per complaint studied with the cause, the fix, who owns it, the due day and the day it was done; the days to fix and the fix check fill in by themselves.
Contract price reviews with the increase
One row per price review of a contract with the day, the old monthly value and the new monthly value; the client, the increase and the extra value per year fill in by themselves.
Notes on office clients with the follow-up
One row per note about an office client with the day, the contact role and the follow-up day; the days to the follow-up and the phone fill in by themselves.
Complaint kinds with the response target
The kinds of complaint with the hours you want to take to reply and the rule for a credit; the complaint sheet reads the target hours from here.
The three crews (the cleaners who work together on a job) and the other groups with the lead and the hours a week; the team lead texts about a complaint or a re-clean go to these leads.
Client milestones with the months since the start
One row per milestone reached by a client (first visit, three months, one year) with the day; the months since the start and the phone fill in by themselves.
Win-back offers with the months since the client left
One row per offer sent to a client who left with the day, the offer and the result; the months since the client left and the phones fill in by themselves.
